output.summary: An uncommon agave of the United States' desert southwest, Utah agave forms rosettes of sharp, blue-green leaves and can grow in clonal colonies. Its very tall flower cluster bears bulbous yellow or yellow-green flowers. Local Native American peoples, including the Havasupai, historically used the plant for food and fibre.
output.edibilityNote: The plant was historically used for food and fibre by local Native American peoples, including the Havasupai; no plant part or preparation is specified.
